reason: Every entry is done, no-effect-yet, later or cannot-occur with evidence. The hit arm has landed: a hero move into a hostile runs uhitm.c hmon() (817-834) and hmon_hitmon() (1752-1935) with the eleven helpers those two reach, and a blow that lands without killing finishes the turn. The kill at hmon_hitmon():1911 and the second attack at hitum():791-812 are excluded by this slice’s own boundary rather than missing from it, and each refuses before output, randomness or state change; both are the goal’s remaining slices.

boundary.startingEvent: a movement keystroke whose destination square holds a hostile monster, and whose to-hit roll at uhitm.c:780 lands
boundary.endingEvent: the screen and cursor at the end of that turn, with the target alive
boundary.validInputs: the eight movement keys and their run and rush forms, with any role, race, gender and alignment; no F force-fight prefix, no ranged attack and no #twoweapon
boundary.observables: the random-number log, the full 24x80 screen with attributes, the cursor, and the persisted mon.mhp, u.uconduct.weaphit, u.weapon_skills[].advance, mon.mstrategy, mon.msleeping and mon.mcanmove
boundary.exclusions: the kill itself at hmon_hitmon():1911 killed(), the second attack at hitum():791-812, force-fight, ranged and applied hits, a polymorphed hero via hmonas(), hero death at js/hack.js losehp()'s u.uhp < 1 branch, monster retaliation via mhitu.c mattacku(), and pet-versus-monster melee via mhitm.c mattackm()

candidateListMethod.upstreamEntryPoints: uhitm.c known_hitum() 585-646 hit arm, hmon() 817-834, hmon_hitmon() 1752-1935. Every function hmon_hitmon() names was read in full: hmon_hitmon_do_hit() 1386-1433, hmon_hitmon_barehands() 837-882, hmon_hitmon_weapon_ranged() 884-918, backstabbable() 920-931, hmon_hitmon_weapon_melee() 933-1067, hmon_hitmon_weapon() 1069-1092, hmon_hitmon_potion() 1094-1116, hmon_hitmon_misc_obj() 1118-1384, hmon_hitmon_dmg_recalc() 1435-1507, hmon_hitmon_poison() 1509-1538, hmon_hitmon_jousting() 1540-1567, hmon_hitmon_stagger() 1569-1585, hmon_hitmon_pet() 1587-1601, hmon_hitmon_splitmon() 1603-1634, hmon_hitmon_msg_hit() 1636-1660, hmon_hitmon_msg_silver() 1662-1699, hmon_hitmon_msg_lightobj() 1701-1751, first_weapon_hit() 1962-1990, m_is_steadfast() 5216-5243 and mhitm_knockback() 5245-5372. Beneath them: weapon.c dmgval() 215-355, special_dmgval() 357-425, dbon() 990-1014, use_skill() 1423-1434, uwep_skill_type() 1531-1537, weapon_dam_bonus() 1638-1729, and artifact.c artifact_light() 2263-2275.
candidateListMethod.dispatchTablesAndCatalogs: hmon_hitmon_do_hit()'s oclass dispatch at 1420-1431 (WEAPON_CLASS, is_weptool, GEM_CLASS, POTION_CLASS, everything else); hmon_hitmon_weapon()'s four ranged tests at 1072-1086; dmgval()'s two otyp switches at 228-262 and 265-295, both transcribed against objects.c rather than summarized; weapon_dam_bonus()'s three skill switches; hmon_hitmon_msg_hit()'s four verbs at 1649-1657; hmon_hitmon_barehands()'s twohits switch at 861-881; include/you.h:511-552, the 27 fields of struct _hitmon_data, ported in declaration order.
candidateListMethod.reachableHelpers: Each helper was traced from hmon_hitmon() outward and its guard read before its body, so a refusal could be placed above the first draw rather than after it. The random-number order was then confirmed against a live replay and against fresh C recordings: rn2(20), rn2(19), rnd(20), rn2(19), the damage die, then either rnd(100) or the rn2(3) and rn2(6) pair, then rn2(25) and rn2(3).
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: `grep -rnwE '(hmon|hmon_hitmon|dmgval|special_dmgval|dbon|weapon_dam_bonus|use_skill|uwep_skill_type|mhitm_knockback|first_weapon_hit)' js/` returned only comments before this slice; the camelCase spelling of each returned 0. `grep -rn 'artifactLight\|artifact_light' js/` returned five separate definitions, which this slice converged onto js/artifacts.js. `grep -rnw 'is_weptool' js/` returns 1 and `isWeptool` 22, so that one was reused rather than ported again; the same check moved `is_flimsy` out of scope, because js/makemon_create.js:2027 already holds a partial port under the camelCase spelling and mhitm_knockback() stops above the line that would read it.
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: Three branches inside the boundary cannot be recorded from a first dungeon level and are pinned by unit test alone: zap.c exclam()'s "!", which needs a blow above four points that the target survives; hmon_hitmon_barehands()'s rnd(4), which needs martial_bonus(); and its silver-ring and blessed-glove bonuses, which need equipment no role starts with. A port-side scan of 6000 Valkyrie, 6000 Barbarian, 5000 Caveman and 4000 Monk seeds found no survivor of a blow above four points, which is the evidence for the first two. hmon_hitmon_msg_hit()'s "bash" verb and the wet-towel half of "lash" were dropped rather than ported, because hmon_hitmon_do_hit() cannot deliver an object that selects either.

entries.reachability: Every swing whose rnd(20) at 780 is beaten, which is roughly half of them. It runs before hmon() and after it: the conduct counter at 615-616 is what hmon_hitmon():1843 tests, and the morale check at 623-631 is drawn only for a survivor.
entries.effects: u.uconduct.weaphit rises by one for a weapon or weapon-tool; rn2(25) is drawn for a survivor. Two arms stop: the morale check's body needs mon.c set_ustuck(), and cutworm() needs a long worm.

entries.reachability: The only entry to hmon_hitmon(). Its own body is two consequences of striking a monster the town protects, and both are refused above the call so neither spends the damage roll first.

sourceReview: Every C span named here was confirmed by printing its first and last line rather than citing it, and the two spans the goal record gave as 819-834 and 1754-1935 are 817-834 and 1752-1935 once the staticfn line above each declaration is counted. All 21 uhitm.c helpers hmon_hitmon() names were read in full, including the six that stop, so that each refusal could be placed above the first draw on its path rather than after it: hmon()'s priest and guard arms sit above hmon_hitmon(); hmon_hitmon_barehands()'s shade arm above its rnd(); hmon_hitmon_weapon_melee()'s artifact, joust and poison arms above the flags they would set; hmon_hitmon_stagger()'s and mhitm_knockback()'s bodies below the draws C makes there, which is the earliest either can be placed. The random-number order was traced through hmon_hitmon() twice, once against a live replay and once against fifteen fresh C recordings, and the two agree call for call. Four terms decided by `hmd.thrown` were folded out rather than restated, because hmon() admits HMON_MELEE alone and dothrow.c, dokick.c and apply.c have no port; each fold is named in a comment beside the code. Two arms of hmon_hitmon_msg_hit() were dropped for the same kind of reason, that hmon_hitmon_do_hit() cannot deliver an object of the class they test for. `js/weapon.js is_flimsy` was deliberately not ported, because js/makemon_create.js:2027 already holds a partial copy and mhitm_knockback() stops one line above the only reader; porting it would have made a second copy of a function the last correctness pass already flagged twice. artifact_light() went the other way: its five existing copies were converged onto js/artifacts.js, with the development score identical session by session across the change.
